title: bug: .moe task JSON persists raw bidi/format characters from tool text
description:
Repro: task-44b44ccac62f4657890f98ff450738c8. Its complete_step(step-2) note and complete_task summary were sent with backslash-u escapes, and the agent tool-call layer decoded the non-control ones. As a result, .moe/tasks/task-44b44ccac62f4657890f98ff450738c8.json now holds literal U+061C, U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E (incl. RLO), U+2060-U+206F and U+FEFF. Board commits stage that file, which triggers GitHub hidden-Unicode / Trojan Source warnings.

Fix idea: have the daemon's .moe JSON writer emit those code points (plus U+2028/U+2029) as JSON escapes. That is byte-safe and value-identical. Add a regression test.
definitionOfDone: Every .moe JSON record the daemon writes encodes U+061C, U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+206F and U+FEFF as JSON escape sequences, so the file bytes contain none of those code points.
Parsed values are unchanged by the escaping (a round-trip test with a U+202E-bearing note/summary).
A test proves a task note/summary containing U+202E is written without the raw character and reads back identical.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first (load test-driven-development). Extend this existing small real-filesystem suite with JSON-persistence describe blocks; keep existing rename-backoff tests unchanged. Use numeric code points only, with the exact target list built as: const cps=[0x061c,...Array.from({length:5},(_,i)=>0x200b+i),...Array.from({length:7},(_,i)=>0x2028+i),...Array.from({length:16},(_,i)=>0x2060+i),0xfeff]; const hidden=String.fromCodePoint(...cps); const slash=String.fromCharCode(92). For BOTH atomicWriteJson and atomicWriteJsonAsync, persist an object containing hidden inside nested values, arrays AND a property name. Assert for every cp: expect(raw.includes(String.fromCodePoint(cp))).toBe(false); expect(raw).toContain(slash+'u'+cp.toString(16).padStart(4,'0')); expect(JSON.parse(raw)).toEqual(input). Repeat writes to expose regex-state leakage. Include an already-literal slash+'u202e' string, quotes/backslashes/newlines, null, empty containers, ordinary Hebrew/Arabic/accented text and emoji plus non-target range neighbors; compare parsed values with JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(input)) and prove non-target Unicode is not ASCII-escaped indiscriminately. Verify atomicWriteText/atomicWriteTextAsync still write their input exactly to .txt targets. Circular and BigInt serialization must throw/reject while leaving an existing target unchanged and no temporary files behind.
Add a real StateManager task-record regression in this same persistence-focused test file using the existing ToolTestHarness (init/setupMoeFolder/createEpic/createTask/load, cleanup in finally): await h.state.updateTask(task.id,{implementationPlan:[{stepId:'step-1',description:'persist note',status:'COMPLETED',affectedFiles:[],note}],completionSummary:summary}); use prefix+String.fromCodePoint(0x202e)+suffix in both fields. Read .moe/tasks/<id>.json, assert no raw RLO and that the escape spelling exists; JSON.parse and a subsequent state.load must retain the exact note and completionSummary. This proves DoD 2/3 at the actual task persistence boundary without mutating the live board.
Also cover the bypass entrypoints from steps 2/3 here: accounts.writeJsonAtomic with the all-code-point nested object (including its trailing newline and POSIX 0600 mode); initProjectTool.handler with an RLO-bearing project name; exported index.initProject with the same name, and exported writeDaemonInfo with an RLO-bearing projectPath (do NOT start a daemon). Mock os.homedir to a temporary home and seed ~/.moe/config.json with an extra RLO-bearing value before index.initProject; verify that value survives escaped in config.json. All raw-file assertions must fail against the current implementation, not merely assert successful parsing. Tests restore mocks and recursively remove temp roots on every exit.
implementationPlan.note: Extended atomicWrite.test.ts (293 lines, LF, ASCII-source numeric code points; numeric scan: zero raw target chars). Ran it in a fresh HEAD archive snapshot /tmp/moe-9c86-gate.* (lockfile JSON-equal to the Linux native node_modules at /tmp/moe-linux-daemon.3EJTl5; MOE_* scrubbed): 10 failed (all escape-dependent: sync/async escape + concurrent/large, task-record round-trip, accounts writeJsonAtomic, moe.init_project, index initProject + global config, writeDaemonInfo not exported, acquireLock) and 8 passed (pre-existing backoff tests + non-target/literal-escape guards, circular/BigInt rejection, byte-exact text writers). Shared checkout has 400+ unrelated dirty paths; untouched.

Added module-private fileJsonFormatChars (built from numeric ranges) and exported escapeJsonForFile in atomicWrite.ts; applied after JSON.stringify in atomicWriteJson and atomicWriteJsonAsync only (text helpers, retry, fsync untouched). accounts/registry.ts writeJsonAtomic wraps only the JSON.stringify (trailing newline, mode 0600, retries unchanged); the import pulls in only fs/path. Both files LF, zero raw target code points. Snapshot run (atomicWrite.test + src/accounts): 47 passed, 4 failing remain by design (moe.init_project, index initProject, writeDaemonInfo export, acquireLock) for step 3.

implementationPlan.description: Close the audited bypasses using the same escapeJsonForFile helper, changing serialized BYTES only. In index.ts wrap JSON.stringify at writeDaemonInfo (.moe/daemon.json), writeGlobalConfig (~/.moe/config.json), initProject (.moe/project.json), and acquireLock's JSON payload (retain its existing compact JSON.stringify call without pretty-printing). Preserve existing temp names, exclusive lock creation, rename ordering, existing error handling and fail-open global-config behavior; do not replace these IO implementations or alter lifecycle logic. Add writeDaemonInfo to the existing lifecycle-helper export list so the regression test calls the actual writer rather than matching source text or launching a live daemon. In tools/initProject.ts wrap both existing JSON.stringify calls for project.json and canonical channel records, preserving force-reinit project identity and channel deduplication. Do not touch HTTP/WS JSON, generated init/skill files, logs or .claude assets. All these are ordinary UTF-8 writes with path.join/Node APIs on Windows/macOS/Linux; no launcher changes or platform-specific shell code are needed. Do not directly edit any existing .moe record or add a migration. The user-approved scope includes both project and machine-level dynamic JSON records.
implementationPlan.note: Wrapped JSON.stringify with escapeJsonForFile at index.ts writeDaemonInfo, writeGlobalConfig, initProject (project.json) and acquireLock (compact form kept); exported writeDaemonInfo; tools/initProject.ts project.json + channel records. No IO/lifecycle changes. Both files LF, zero raw target code points. Snapshot: atomicWrite/index/initProject/accounts tests 6 files 67 passed 1 skipped; tsc --noEmit OK. Residual non-escaped JSON writers left deliberately out of scope per plan: chatStore JSONL messages (runtime, gitignored), claudeHook .claude/settings.json, test harness fixtures.

implementationPlan.description:
One final verification gate for this shared persistence change: run full daemon regression and typecheck (broader than normal mid-epic coverage because all record families share the writer). Exact evidence command from repository root:
cd packages/moe-daemon && node --input-type=module -e "import {spawnSync} from 'node:child_process'; import path from 'node:path'; const env={...process.env}; for(const k of Object.keys(env)) if(k.startsWith('MOE_')) delete env[k]; if(process.platform!=='win32') env.PATH=[path.dirname(process.execPath),'/usr/local/bin','/usr/bin','/bin'].join(':'); for(const args of [['node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc','--noEmit'],['node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs','run']]) {const r=spawnSync(process.execPath,args,{env,stdio:'inherit'}); if(r.error) throw r.error; if(r.status!==0) process.exit(r.status??1);}"

This portable Node wrapper scrubs inherited MOE_* seat bindings and uses native-only PATH on POSIX so accounts subprocess tests do not inherit Windows executables. Use an isolated source snapshot with native Linux npm-ci dependencies when the shared node_modules belongs to Windows: preserve package-lock.json and source hashes, include root CLAUDE.md, scripts, docs and package files required by daemon contract tests, and do not install over shared Windows dependencies or hand-edit dist/generated files. On native Windows the same command uses process.execPath and preserves Windows PATH; no GNU env dependency. Do not treat unrelated shared-tree failures as evidence of success; attribute them and rerun against a stable snapshot containing this task's changes.

implementationPlan.description: Exactly one final adversarial self-review (load adversarial-self-review) scoped to this diff. Audit every target-range endpoint, property names/nested arrays, multiple writes and concurrent async calls, pre-existing literal escape text, null/empty/large inputs, surrogate pairs and valid non-target Unicode. Prove escaping happens after JSON.stringify and does not change values, transport bytes, digests, atomicity, error propagation or account permissions. Re-audit the dynamic filesystem JSON callsites to ensure startup/init/account bypasses use the helper; bundled static assets and JSONL/logs are not a hidden migration. Read the task-record round-trip assertions as an attacker: removal of either sync or async escaping or loss of a target range must make tests fail. Scan the five modified source/test files numerically for any raw target code point (including comments and test fixtures); the implementation and notes must contain none. Confirm no direct .moe changes, generated edits, unrelated dirty bytes or Git writes were introduced. If fixes are needed, rerun the SAME verification command before completion and report all modified paths. Hand off via complete_task for independent QA; do not claim runtime rollout/restart or trusted-runner certification.
implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review done. Escaping runs after JSON.stringify; target chars can only occur inside JSON strings/keys, so the escape is always valid and value-identical; regex has no u flag and targets BMP only, so surrogate pairs/emoji untouched; escape is computed before any tmp file is created so circular/BigInt reject cleanly. Review fix: added a backslash-directly-before-target-char case to the test sample (backslashed). 18 mutation probes in scratch copies (drop sync escape, drop async escape, shrink each of the 5 range endpoints, drop each bypass: registry, writeDaemonInfo, writeGlobalConfig, index initProject, tool initProject, acquireLock, wrong escape prefix, unpadded hex) each turn atomicWrite.test.ts red (1-11 failures each). Numeric scan of the 5 files: zero raw target code points, all LF. Re-audit of dynamic JSON writers: remaining unescaped are deliberate out-of-scope per plan: chatStore/activityLog JSONL (runtime, gitignored), claudeHook .claude/settings.json, test harness fixtures. Channel record escape in tools/initProject.ts is defense in depth (canonical names, not directly testable). No .moe, generated, dist edits; no Git writes; 400+ peer-dirty paths untouched. Reran the SAME gate after the test tweak in fresh snapshot: tsc exit 0, vitest 153 files / 3422 passed / 9 skipped, exit 0 (/tmp/moe-9c86-gate2.log).

reopenReason: Feed-in-order rule (human-approved): no prerequisites. Daemon .moe JSON writer bug filed by worker-c1d9de02 from the CQ-M03a fix; board commits currently carry raw bidi/BOM characters (task-44b44cca's record).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Escape only after JSON.stringify, including property names and nested values. Reject stripping/rejecting tool input, escaping in complete_step alone, recursively mutating objects, or patching historical .moe files. Keep raw text writers untouched because roles/scripts/copied assets are not JSON state records. Keep account writer permissions, trailing newline and standalone CLI operation; import only the stateless fs/path utility, never daemon state, tools or logger.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
# JSON file format-character escaping Implementation Plan
Goal: eliminate the specified raw invisible characters from daemon-written JSON bytes without changing parsed values. Architecture: one ASCII-source, stateless post-JSON.stringify escaping helper; use it in both shared atomic JSON writers and the audited startup/init/account bypasses. Tech stack: TypeScript/Node ESM, Vitest. User explicitly confirmed inclusion of machine-level ~/.moe account/config JSON in the REPL. This is a focused bugfix, not CQ-M whole-system rollout. Reproduced with JSON.stringify({completionSummary:'note'+String.fromCodePoint(0x202e)}): serializedStillHasRawRLO=true, roundTrips=true. persistence.writeEntity delegates to atomicWriteJsonAsync; project normalization, pins and decisions also use the shared atomic JSON helpers. Other dynamic JSON writes are in index.ts, initProject.ts and accounts/registry.ts. No schema or wire-value changes.
planningNotes.risks: All five owned files were clean, i/lf w/lf at planning; shared checkout has substantial unrelated dirt. Preserve peer bytes and EOLs, and leave all Git writes to wrappers on designated moe/work-2026-10-24 (no direct main push). All fixtures must use temp project/home directories, never live .moe or the operator's home. The tool layer may decode source-style Unicode escape text: use numeric code points in tool notes/tests and byte-scan source. Do not bulk-migrate historical records; they become escaped on next normal write. JSONL message/activity logs, daemon.lock filename semantics, static bundled JSON assets and .claude configuration are not new storage formats in this task; encode the lock's JSON payload too while preserving its compact form and O_EXCL semantics. Shared helper usage must not change JSON wire output, stable candidate digests or in-memory strings.

completionSummary: Daemon-written .moe JSON files no longer contain the hidden/format code points U+061C, U+200B-200F, U+2028-202E, U+2060-206F and U+FEFF. They are written as lowercase 4-digit JSON escape sequences, so parsed values are identical. New exported escapeJsonForFile in util/atomicWrite.ts is applied after JSON.stringify in atomicWriteJson and atomicWriteJsonAsync (covers keys, nested values and arrays; text helpers, retry, fsync and error propagation untouched). The same helper closes the direct writers: accounts/registry.ts writeJsonAtomic (newline and 0600 mode kept), index.ts writeDaemonInfo (now exported), writeGlobalConfig, initProject and the compact acquireLock payload, and tools/initProject.ts project.json plus channel records. Tests: util/atomicWrite.test.ts grew to 18 tests covering the sync and async writers, concurrent and large writes, circular and BigInt rejection with the target untouched, byte-exact text writers, a real StateManager task-record round trip of a U+202E note and summary, and every bypass writer. 18 mutation probes (drop either escape, shrink each range endpoint, drop each bypass) all turn the file red. Out of scope per the plan: JSONL logs, claudeHook .claude/settings.json, and historical records, which are not migrated and are escaped on their next normal write. Not claiming runtime rollout, a daemon restart or trusted-runner certification.
